verdict.rationale: ReadMe's own docs say it generates interactive API reference pages from an uploaded OpenAPI (OAS) file, and that API definitions can live in Git. However, no evidence shows that reference pages automatically update when the spec changes. Git-based workflows and bi-directional sync are described only at a high level, and the rdme CLI is documented without any spec-sync details. missing for 10: explicit documentation that reference pages auto-update on spec changes (e.g., CI/CLI spec sync or webhook-triggered regeneration), details on how spec updates propagate, independent or hands-on corroboration of sync behavior.

support.subject: As a developer, my API reference pages are generated from an OpenAPI spec and stay in sync when the spec changes

citations.quote: ReadMe makes it simple to transform your existing OAS file into beautiful, interactive documentation that your developers will actually enjoy using.
Get your API documentation live in three steps: create a project, upload your API definition, and write your first guide.
Run documentation entirely through Git, with Markdown and OpenAPI in your repository and pull requests as the review step.
Bi-directional sync creates a two-way connection between your ReadMe project and a GitHub or GitLab repository.
